authority.decision_basis: The incumbent has bounded marginal graph cost and no active C compilation, while replacement would assume mature cross-platform async-signal-safe registration, handler chaining, lifecycle, Windows event, and process-authority obligations. Current defects are material but repairable while retaining the incumbent, and the required cross-platform runtime baselines do not exist.

semantic_matrix.observed: Unix signal-hook iterator uses async-signal-safe registration and a self-pipe; Windows uses low-level CRT handlers and Win32 events. Asupersync fans recorded emissions out by kind.
semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: Recorded dispatcher emissions are delivered to streams; raw OS arrival cardinality is not preserved.

semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: coalescing is allowed before the Asupersync counter

semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: no total cross-kind order is promised

semantic_matrix.observed: dispatcher counters preserve repeated iterator emissions; upstream pending collation can reduce raw arrivals; shutdown listeners exit after first observed event
semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: repeated escalation behavior differs by surface

semantic_matrix.observed: the global dispatcher and its thread live for the process; shutdown and reload add detached threads; reload can remain blocked after controller drop until another signal
semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: listener cancellation does not unregister process handlers or join all listener threads

semantic_matrix.contract_boundary: first registration changes OS disposition for the process lifetime

gaps.finding: Signal::recv documentation says no delivered notification is lost without stating that signal-hook and the OS may coalesce raw arrivals.
the first Unix listener eagerly registers all ten kinds and changes default disposition for unrelated signals
global and controller listener threads/registrations are not joined or unregistered on listener cancellation; reload can outlive its controller until another signal
Windows CRT signal registration has race and semantic limitations, and source-token tests do not prove console-control delivery
atpd stop and reload signal a PID-file value without process identity fencing; PID reuse can target an unrelated process
raw kill, sysinfo kill_with, taskkill, and Child signaling expose divergent permission, absence, timeout, escalation, and error semantics
macOS, supported BSD, and Windows lack fresh runtime delivery and lifecycle receipts
several tests described as real signal or e2e drive controller state or inject internal emissions instead of exercising OS delivery
the three CAP-SIGNALS dependency-sovereignty scenarios and the registry command are planned but not implemented by the runner
fork-after-registration and child reinitialization behavior are untested and explicitly unclaimed
the capability registry source-owner list omits shutdown, graceful, CLI signal, process, and daemon_control surfaces
unsafe ledger locators have source drift and broad file-level unsafe scopes remain in atpd and process

reconsideration_triggers.required_evidence: minimal reproduction, upstream disposition, affected-platform runtime receipt, and owner review

reconsideration_triggers.required_evidence: delivery, coalescing, ordering, repeated, lifetime, handler chaining, masks, fork, process permission, stale PID, cancellation, and teardown receipts

decision.required_next_action: Route the thirteen gaps as incumbent hardening or proof work. Do not begin replacement design or implementation unless a reconsideration trigger produces a new owner-reviewed gate.
decision.rollback: No source or dependency change was made; retain the incumbent and this inventory as the claim-time baseline.

no_claim_boundaries: This inventory does not prove raw OS arrival cardinality, total ordering, or absence of coalescing.
Linux source and test evidence does not prove macOS, BSD, or Windows runtime behavior.
Static Windows token checks do not prove console-control delivery, races, or teardown.
A Unix self-pipe design does not cover Windows control events or process permission and liveness semantics.
Modeled controller transitions and injected dispatcher emissions are not real-process signal E2E evidence.
The one real child SIGTERM send journey does not prove signal receive parity.
This inventory does not prove fork safety, PID identity safety, or uniform permission classification.
The marginal graph ledger does not prove runtime correctness, release readiness, or performance.
DEFER does not bless current defects; it routes them without authorizing dependency replacement.
No file deletion, dependency removal, replacement child, or cutover is authorized.
